Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend who has just started assembling furniture asks for a quick video call because the instructions are confusing.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: A notice has been posted about an optional training session happening next week.
Story:
I was on my lunch break at the construction site, boots caked in dust, when my phone buzzed. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his message frantic: “Can you hop on a quick video call? I’m losing my mind with this bookshelf.” I could picture him, surrounded by planks and screws, frustration written all over his face. As a friend, I knew he counted on me, especially since he’d just moved out on his own. I wanted to be there for him, to help him through this small but meaningful struggle.

But just then, the foreman walked by, pinning up a notice about next week’s optional training session. He caught my eye and nodded, making it clear he expected me to sign up. “We need everyone on board for safety updates,” he said. I knew the team relied on me to pull my weight, to show commitment and not slack off. The pressure to be a dependable worker pressed down on me, just as the urge to be a supportive friend tugged from the other side. My thumb hovered over the call button, heart pounding, torn between the two worlds that needed me.
